Caps how long a single response can be — lower is faster and more battery-friendly on phone hardware.

Breaks your question into sub-questions, researches each separately, then synthesizes one answer. Several sequential model calls on the same model — noticeably slower than a normal reply, not multiple AI models running at once. Independent from the response style above: it changes how much research goes into an answer, not its tone — the two combine (e.g. Deep Research + Succinct still synthesizes a short final answer).

Classifies each message and picks which downloaded model answers it (e.g. a lightweight model for small talk, a stronger one for research/comparison questions), switching between them as needed. On by default and independent from Deep Research — if it fails for any reason, chat falls back to your normal active model automatically, it never leaves you without a response.

Import your own .txt, .md, .csv, .json, or .pdf notes — indexed on this device only, never uploaded anywhere. PDFs need selectable text (scanned/image-only pages won\'t extract — there\'s no OCR), and password-protected PDFs aren\'t supported.

BOAR is an offline-first mobile AI system exploring adaptive model routing, local retrieval, and resource-aware inference. It performs local LLM inference via llama.rn / llama.cpp and local hybrid retrieval (SQLite FTS5 + on-device embeddings) with zero cloud dependencies.
Complies with strict mobile field constraints: resident memory remains capped under 12GB RAM using memory-mapped weights (mmap), and total storage is audited against a 50GB storage envelope.

BOAR measures every answer on your own phone: model load time, time to first token, tokens/sec, peak memory and which sources were used. Run the built-in evaluation from Execution Telemetry → 🧪 Evaluate to compare any installed model on the same questions, or run it from a computer over adb (see AGENTS.md on GitHub).
